solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

passage_flags: minor: passage is ~420 words, well short of a typical ACT Reading passage (~700-900 words).

minor: 'killed thousands of people' understates Tambora's toll (roughly 10,000+ direct deaths, tens of thousands more from famine and disease); not false, but 'tens of thousands' would be more accurate.

flags: minor: 'what they reveal about climate' is a bit loose; the passage's lesson is about averages vs. timing of cold, but B is still clearly best.
R024-01.notes: Passage traces Tambora's far-off effects and the lesson that averages hide timing. A is unsupported, C is contradicted by the last paragraph, D is not a comparison the passage makes.

R024-02.notes: Para 2 states it directly: the sulfur haze reflected sunlight back into space. C (sunspots) is a trap from para 3, but it is clearly what people mistakenly blamed.

R024-03.notes: 'Modest ... less than one degree' means small. 'Humble' is the familiar-meaning trap but is easy to reject.

flags: minor: overlaps somewhat with R024-06 (both depend on the 'small average, big harm' idea).
R024-04.notes: Para 3 gives snow in June, frosts, rotted harvests, riots, which illustrate 'averages can hide a great deal.' B is contradicted (Europe is also mentioned).

flags: minor: billed as an inference, but it is nearly a restatement of 'no one yet understood how a volcano could change the weather', so it plays as a detail question.
R024-05.notes: Few had heard of the eruption and no one understood the mechanism, so people blamed sunspots or luck. A and D are contradicted.

R024-06.notes: Para 4: the timing of the cold matters more than the drop in the mean, because frosts in the growing season destroy crops. B contradicts 'less than one degree'. C distorts the hypothetical 'winter several degrees colder'. The B and C traps may catch some readers, which puts it at the easy/medium border.

flags: Overlap/giveaway: D ('qualify a popular claim about it') points straight at R024-08's answer (skeptical of the 'volcano produced the novel' claim), and R024-08 likewise confirms R024-07's D.
R024-07.notes: The last paragraph adds the Frankenstein episode, then qualifies the 'volcano produced the novel' story. B is an overstatement, and A and C are off topic.

flags: minor: B nearly quotes the passage ('the weather supplied the occasion; the ideas were already Shelley's own'), so it is a near-verbatim match and very easy.
R024-08.notes: The author calls the claim tempting but says it is more accurate to credit the weather with the occasion only. C and D attribute claims the author never makes.
